notes:
I couldn't write the notes this time, because I wasn't able to read any of the source pages.

I tried to open six pages in one step: Enduring Word on Psalm 136, the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit commentaries on BibleHub, Augustine's exposition on New Advent and the NET Bible notes. Something came back, but my code failed before it showed me the text. That was my mistake. The tool then stopped letting me make more requests in this turn, so I never saw what any of those pages say on this psalm.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without anything read, I can't give you a single properly sourced verse note, so I've left the notes out rather than guess.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these pages:
- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word's Psalm 136 commentary; Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on BibleHub, StudyLight or CCEL; and Precept Austin's Psalm 136 page.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus any Psalm 136 material on Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, LCMS and 1517. I'll only report real differences that I find. On a praise psalm like this there may be few.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes (for example, on the Hebrew word *hesed* and the "Red Sea" or "Sea of Reeds" question in v. 13) and Bible Odyssey. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, Augustine's exposition on New Advent (numbered Psalm 135 in the old Latin and Greek Bibles), Catholic.com and OCA (on this psalm's use in Orthodox worship). For debated modern teaching, I'll check whether the allowed sites tie v. 25 ("He gives food to every creature") to prosperity teaching. I'll only include this if a site actually says it.
